Package neqsim.mathlib.linearalgebra

Class ApacheCommonsMathLinearAlgebra

java.lang.Object
neqsim.mathlib.linearalgebra.ApacheCommonsMathLinearAlgebra
All Implemented Interfaces:
LinearAlgebraOperations
public final class ApacheCommonsMathLinearAlgebra extends Object implements LinearAlgebraOperations
LinearAlgebraOperations backed by Apache Commons Math.

Square solves and inversion use LU decomposition, least squares uses QR decomposition, and rank and conditioning use a singular value decomposition. Backend performance depends on matrix size, operation and runtime; select a backend using representative benchmarks.

    • solve

      public double[] solve(double[][] matrixA, double[] vectorB)
      Solve the square system A x = b.

      Uses LU without a numerical rank or conditioning threshold. An ill-conditioned matrix can yield a finite but inaccurate result, even when LinearAlgebraOperations.rank(double[][]) reports numerical rank deficiency. Use LinearAlgebraOperations.conditionNumber(double[][]) and residual checks to assess suitability for the caller's accuracy target.

      Specified by:
      solve in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrixA - square coefficient matrix
      vectorB - right-hand-side vector with one entry per row of matrixA
      Returns:
      the solution vector

    • solveLeastSquares

      public double[] solveLeastSquares(double[][] matrixA, double[] vectorB)
      Solve A x = b in the least-squares sense, minimising the Euclidean norm of the residual.

      Use this for over-determined systems from parameter fitting with full column rank. Rank-deficient systems are rejected; this method is not a pseudoinverse fallback. For a well-conditioned square system it returns the same answer as LinearAlgebraOperations.solve(double[][], double[]) but generally costs more.

      Specified by:
      solveLeastSquares in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrixA - coefficient matrix with at least as many rows as columns
      vectorB - right-hand-side vector with one entry per row of matrixA
      Returns:
      the least-squares solution, one entry per column of matrixA

    • invert

      public double[][] invert(double[][] matrix)
      Compute the inverse of a square matrix.

      Prefer LinearAlgebraOperations.solve(double[][], double[]) when the inverse is only needed to multiply a right-hand side; an explicit inverse is both slower and numerically weaker. Use this only when the inverse itself is the result, as in a covariance or sensitivity matrix. As with LinearAlgebraOperations.solve(double[][], double[]), no numerical rank or conditioning threshold is applied; a finite inverse can still be inaccurate for an ill-conditioned matrix.

      Specified by:
      invert in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - square matrix to invert
      Returns:
      the inverse matrix

      public double[] subtract(double[] vectorA, double[] vectorB)

    • rank

      public int rank(double[][] matrix)
      Determine the numerical rank of a matrix.

      The rank is the number of singular values above a tolerance scaled by the largest singular value and the matrix dimensions, so a matrix that is singular only to within rounding error is reported as rank deficient.

      Specified by:
      rank in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - matrix of any shape
      Returns:
      the numerical rank, between zero and the smaller of the two dimensions

    • conditionNumber

      public double conditionNumber(double[][] matrix)
      Compute the two-norm condition number, the ratio of the largest to the smallest singular value.

      A value near one indicates a well-conditioned matrix. A value comparable with the reciprocal of machine epsilon, about 1.0e16 in double precision, means a solution carries no significant digits.

      Specified by:
      conditionNumber in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - matrix of any shape
      Returns:
      the condition number, or Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY if the matrix is numerically rank deficient, using the same tolerance as LinearAlgebraOperations.rank(double[][])

    • determinant

      public double determinant(double[][] matrix)
      Compute the determinant of a square matrix.

      A determinant is a poor test for singularity because it scales with the size of the entries; prefer LinearAlgebraOperations.conditionNumber(double[][]) or LinearAlgebraOperations.rank(double[][]) for that. Use this where the determinant itself is the quantity of interest.

      Specified by:
      determinant in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - square matrix
      Returns:
      the determinant

    • spectralNorm

      public double spectralNorm(double[][] matrix)
      Compute the induced two-norm of a matrix, which is its largest singular value.

      This requires a singular value decomposition and so costs far more than LinearAlgebraOperations.oneNorm(double[][]). For a single-column matrix it equals the Euclidean length, but LinearAlgebraOperations.euclideanNorm(double[]) computes that directly and should be preferred inside an iteration.

      Specified by:
      spectralNorm in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - matrix to measure
      Returns:
      the spectral norm

    • eigenDecomposition

      public RealEigenDecomposition eigenDecomposition(double[][] matrix)
      Compute paired real eigenvalues and column eigenvectors without imposing an ordering.

      This operation is restricted to real spectra. Complex eigenvalues must not be silently projected onto the real axis. Eigenvectors need not form an invertible basis for a defective matrix.

      Specified by:
      eigenDecomposition in interface LinearAlgebraOperations
      Parameters:
      matrix - finite square matrix
      Returns:
      independent paired eigenvalue and eigenvector arrays satisfying A V = V diag(lambda)

    • realBlockEigenDecomposition

      public RealBlockEigenDecomposition realBlockEigenDecomposition(double[][] matrix)
      Compute the real block representation of a real matrix with a real or complex spectrum.

      This Commons Math extension retains imaginary parts and the associated real block basis. Unlike the strict eigenDecomposition(double[][]) operation, it supports conjugate eigenpairs. Callers must explicitly decide how to use the two-by-two blocks; the basis columns are not individual real eigenvectors for such pairs.

      Parameters:
      matrix - finite square matrix
      Returns:
      immutable real and imaginary eigenvalue parts and real block basis satisfying A V = V D
      Throws:
      LinearAlgebraException - if input is invalid or decomposition fails

    • withSubmatrix

      public double[][] withSubmatrix(double[][] matrix, int firstRow, int firstColumn, double[][] block)
      Copy a matrix with a rectangular block overwritten.

      The argument is left untouched, unlike the in-place block assignment the backends offer. The extent written is given by the dimensions of block, whose top-left corner lands on firstRow, firstColumn.
